Grade positions in PRODUCAO_PROG_PROD/PRODUCAO_ORDEM_COR/COMPRAS_PRODUTO are generic, up to 48 (P1..P48/O1..O48/CO1..CO48/CE1..CE48), not fixed at 6 or 7 — the real position count per grade is defined in PRODUTOS_TAMANHOS.NUMERO_TAMANHOS, keyed by PRODUTOS.GRADE
PRODUTOS.GRADE matches the spreadsheet's GRADE_ATUAL column exactly ('36-44') for all 39 products in Production (30/39 in SOMA_DESENV — DEV's product catalog was incomplete)
For GRADE='36-44', PRODUTOS_TAMANHOS.TAMANHO_1..5 = 36,38,40,42,44 — size 34 is absent from any position of this grade, identically in Development and Production (not a DEV/PROD drift)

Alternative grade codes already registered in Linx include size 34 combined with 36-44 (e.g. '36 - 44 - 34' with TAMANHO_6=34, plus '34-44', '34-42', '34-46' etc.) — the model supports this scenario via a distinct grade code, not a position write on the existing grade

For 77/77 spreadsheet rows, current production quantity (sizes 36-44) equals requested quantity (sizes 36-44) plus the requested size-34 quantity — the operation is a grade rebalance (reallocation), not a volume change

LX_ANM_AJUSTA_PROGRAMACAO_PROD's UPDATE on PRODUCAO_PROG_PROD and the historical SQL's UPDATE on COMPRAS_PRODUTO both omit a column that is part of the real primary key (ENTREGA_INICIAL / ENTREGA respectively) — if multiple rows exist per PROGRAMACAO+PRODUTO+COR_PRODUTO (or PEDIDO+PRODUTO+COR_PRODUTO), the same delta would be applied to all of them

LX_ANM_AJUSTA_PROGRAMACAO_PROD never checks how many rows its UPDATE affected — a 0-row match (PROG target does not exist) still returns EXECUTADO=1/'EXECUTADO COM SUCESSO'; correct PROG/OP/PED classification requires priority OP > PED > PROG applied before calling any procedure, not the procedure's own return value

All 4 procedures (LX_ANM_GERA_OS_ALTERACAO_PCP, LX_ANM_AJUSTA_PROGRAMACAO_PROD, LX_MOVIMENTA_COMPRAS_PA, LX_RECALCULO_RESERVA_MATERIAIS) are byte-for-byte identical between Development and Production; none appear obsolete
